newSounds: e is a short schwa (like the a in about), not Telugu ఎ; ng has no hard g; a final k is a glottal stop; r is trilled like Telugu ర
rhythm: syllable-timed, every syllable pronounced clearly — close to Telugu, so the rhythm is easy for you
registerFirst: Anda (polite you) and saya (polite I). Use bapak/ibu as honorifics; kamu and aku are only for friends
trap: no conjugation and no gender; tidak negates verbs and adjectives, bukan negates nouns; kapan means when
